findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival and throughout the inspection there was not a CFPM available at the facility. The PIC was instructed to have enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts in the facility. A hand out with the current courses known by this department was given to the PIC during the inspection to help facilitate enough CFPMs moving forward. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts where foods and food contact surfaces are being handled and/or prepared.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). 

When asked during the inspection the PIC could not provide reporting agreements or similar paperwork for any of the staff observed in the facility. Signed copies were found for other staff only. Fresh copies of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreements were given to the PIC and signed during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all required paperwork is maintained in the facility at all times and updated as new staff is hired.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

On arrival there was not signage observed at either the kitchen or bathroom hand sinks. Signage was given during the inspection and put up to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all hand sinks maintain signage designating them as intended for hand washing only at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

The spray bottle identified as sanitizer in the dry storage and cleaning area of the facility bleached out the inspector’s test strips. This indicates a concentration capable of leaving harmful residues on food contact surfaces. Education was conducted and the bottle remade during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13(A) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed in a manner as described in sections A-E of this code. 

At the time of this inspection packages of beef are observed in a pan thawing at room temperature. The PIC was consulted and instructed to educate staff as to safe thawing practices. The items were moved to the sink and water turned on to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

During this inspection a sanitizer was not observed ready for use in the prep area. The PIC was consulted a sani bucket made with CL to correct. Ensure that a sanitizer is available for use at all times that foods are being prepared in the facility.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

Test strips are not available for the sanitizers used in the facility. The PIC is instructed to have test strips available for the sanitizers used prior to the follow up.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

Multiple rodent droppings are observed in the dry storage area of the facility. Droppings are restricted to one area and no other signs of pests are observed during this inspection. Cleaning was discussed and the PIC instructed to clean prior to the next routine inspection and maintain clean moving forward.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

An employee drink is observed on a wire shelf above foods and single service items. The PIC was shown and education conducted. The items was removed to correct. Ensure that all personal foods are stored that they do not pose a contamination concern for consumer products/foods.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

On arrival only one reporting agreement is observed signed for food handlers at the facility. Approximately 5 are needed to be compliant. The available food handlers signed copies during this inspection to correct the violation. No further follow-ups will be needed at this time.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment: The reporting agreements have not been completed at this time. The PIC during this inspection stated that the owner/manger lost access to the email that it was sent to previously. The reporting agreements given out by this department will be sent to the new email address given during this inspection today. Another follow-up is being set for 10 days to ensure complaince. sharksfoodmart100@gamil.com

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Reporting agreements are not available for employees at the facility. The SCDPH Reporting Agreements given out by this department are being attached to the email version of this report that will be sent out in the morning.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and the PIC instructed to ensure that safe hand washing takes place at the facility at all times. A barrier should be used to turn off the faucet to protect the freshly cleaned hands from re-contamination.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment:
3-201.11: (A)-(B) FOOD shall be obtained from APPROVED source and not from private home. 

A shoe box with brownies is observed on a shelf in the facility. When asked, the PIC indicated that they are sometimes sold to customers and are made at home. This practice should cease immediately. Foods cannot be prepared at home and brought to the facility for sale. This was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to stop immediately.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-304.15: (A) If used, SINGLE-USE gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD or with raw animal FOOD, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation. 

An employee was observed to manipulate their phone and go back to food preparation activities without changing their gloves. Education was conducted and the gloves changed to correct. Ensure that safe glove use is being enforced throughout the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

The blade of the can opener is observed heavily soiled with dried on debris. The PIC was consulted and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. The can opener was moved to dish for cleaning.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) Multiple pans are observed stored with food debris still contaminating them. 2) Knives stored “ready for use” are observed soiled with food debris. Both situations appear to be related to the items not being effectively cleaned when washed. These items were shown to the PIC and they were instructed to have them rewashed. The items were moved to dish for recleaning to correct the immediate violation. A discussion should be had with the dish washers and over site conducted to ensure that the food contact items are being effectively cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. 

The prep cooler across from the fryers is observed with the lid open throughout this inspection. Diced tomatoes were temped with the probe sitting on the bottom of the pan and a temperature of 46F. Beef patties are observed with internal temperatures of 55F in this same cooler. Per the PIC these items were stocked at 10:30 am. Per code they can be out of temperature for six hours without temperature control so long as they remain under 70F. These items will be used or discarded by 4:30 pm. This issue appears to be an issue of procedure and not the equipment as the bottom section of the cooler is observed in the mid 30s. Education was conducted and the lid will be maintained closed moving forward. The PIC is aware that if this issue persists the TCS foods will begin to be discarded.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. 

1) A half gallon of milk is observed with a date of 6/5/24 (yesterday). 2) Multiple pints of chocolate milk are observed with dates of 5/26/24. These items were shown to the PIC and they were instructed to discard them. These items were removed during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that dates are checked regularly so that items can be used or discarded as needed.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service.

A box of chicken is observed sitting on a shelf in the back room. Per the PIC it is being left out to begin the thawing process. This is a poor practice and needs to cease. Safe thawing practices were discussed. The box was moved to the standing cooler to correct today’s violations. Use safe thawing practices moving forward.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor.

Multiple knives are stored on a magnetic strip in the prep area that is soiled with food debris. This was shown to the PIC. The knives were moved to dish for recleaning and the strip washed/sanitized to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools. 

The mop is observed stored with the head pooled in the mop bucket. Dirty water is observed. Storage was discussed and the mop stored so that it drips dry.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Multiple glove changes were observed during this inspection without hand washing taking place. Education was conducted. Ensure that hand washing takes place at any time that it is required throughout service.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Paper towels were not available at the hand sink during this inspection. Paper towels were placed by the sink almost immediately at the beginning of the inspection. Ensure paper towels are available at the hand sinks at all times foods are being handled.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools. 

The mop is observed stored with the head pooled in the mop bucket. Dirty water is observed. Storage was discussed and the mop stored so that it drips dry.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
PIC was unaware of a written policy for handling vomit or diarrhea in the kitchen. If one exists, PIC did not know where to find it. CORRECTED— Inspector provided a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy. Keep document on hand (in file or posted in the kitchen) for reference if vomit/diarrhea clean up is needed.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Employee trail mix observed in an open bag and a small portion cup on the kitchen counter. CORRECTED— Discussed with employee and PIC. Personal food removed from food prep area.
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No paper towels available at the handwashing sink upon inspector’s arrival at the facility. CORRECTED— PIC and employee provided paper towels. Towels must be provided at handwashing sinks at all times.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Sanitizer was made to a concentration too strong (bleached out inspector’s test strip). CORRECTED— Employee and inspector worked together to make a Cl sanitizer with appropriate concentration (50-200ppm).
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Provide a chlorine test kit for your bleach product. PIC could not locate Cl test strips during inspection.
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: No sanitizer prepared at time of inspection. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC. Sanitizer was created. Sanitizer must be prepared and available at all times of food prep and service (any time food handling may occur).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: The following maintenance concerns should be addressed: seal bare wood around frontline counter food service.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]
